title: fix(runtime): a dispatcher door is served only by the request's own kernel
body:
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:托管多环境主机上,登录、评论、审批链接页、Webhook 重投、入站自动化钩子等入口只由本次请求所在环境自己的服务来处理;该环境没装对应插件时,入口如实回答"尚未提供"。单环境部署用户无感。
- 为什么做:加固多环境部署下这几个入口的服务归属规则。
- 出错会怎样:最坏是某环境里本应可用的入口回答"尚未提供",不会写错数据;改动小,可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么:无

## What changes

A dispatcher door is served only by the request's own kernel.

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts` gains `readDoorSlot`, the reader dispatcher doors read their services through. It reads the slot off the request's own kernel (`getRequestKernelService`, the reader the personal-view, attachment and print bridges already used) and treats a lookup that throws as an empty slot. It carries the same two overloads `getRequestKernelService` has: a slot in `ServiceSlotContracts` reads as its contract, any other name as an untyped value the caller casts.
- The auth door (`auth.ts`), the comment doors (`comments.ts`), the approval action page (`approvals.ts`), the webhook redeliver door (`webhooks.ts`) and the inbound automation hook (`automation-hooks.ts`) now read their member through it, and so does the engine that judges a qualified inbound hook's address. A request kernel without the slot answers the door's existing typed not-available answer, `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, in the request's language, exactly as an empty slot already did.
- The jsdoc of `getRequestKernelService` (`packages/runtime/src/domain-handler-registry.ts`) points doors at `readDoorSlot`.
- On a host with one kernel the request's kernel is that kernel, so nothing changes there.

First files to read, by risk:

1. `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts` — `readDoorSlot` and its overloads, the only new code path.
2. `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts` — the two reader swaps in `handleInboundHookRequest` (the member, and the qualified hook's engine).
3. `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.test.ts` — the last top-level `describe`.

## Tests

A top-level `describe` in `own-door-bridge.test.ts` (the door bridges' shared harness), "a dispatcher door is served only by the request's own kernel", driven through the real `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` with a `kernel-resolver` that places each request on its own kernel:

- for each of eight doors (auth, comments, approvals, webhooks, automation-hooks, personal-views, attachments, print), twice (a request kernel whose lookup throws, and one that answers nothing): the door answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and a member registered elsewhere is never called (16 cases);
- for each of the eight: with the slot on the request kernel, the request kernel's member serves the call (8 preservation cases);
- a qualified inbound hook: a request kernel without the automation engine never consults another kernel's engine for the address, and with its own engine that engine judges it (2 cases);
- the door net: every non-test module under `src/domains/` (any depth) that takes the transport's request whole (`context.request as Request`) or is built on the shared bridge body reads no service through `deps.resolveService`, `deps.resolveServiceOrLoud`, `deps.getService` or a `deps.getObjectQL` given an environment id, and each one that reads a slot itself reads it through `readDoorSlot`; the modules are found by scanning, with a floor of the nine shipped door modules. Not covered, and said so in the pin: a module that hands the request on some other way, and anything outside `src/domains/`. The pin also holds that the reader reads the request kernel's slot and nothing else.

Reverse verification (each leg on the committed fix, mutated through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, then restored and proved byte-identical to `HEAD`):

- the qualified hook's engine read through its previous reader: 2 red (the engine pin and the door net), 75 green;
- the auth door's member read through its previous reader: 1 red (the door net), 76 green;
- earlier round: the four bridge member reads reverted, 9 red; `readDoorSlot` itself reading through another reader, 15 red.

The next commit (`bded79bb60a`, jsdoc and test-comment wording only) rewords it; `own-door-bridge.test.ts` there: `Tests 77 passed (77)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- The preservation cases are green before and after the fix by design: they pin that the request kernel's own member keeps serving.
- No shared-kernel (scoped-registration) mode is affected: every slot these doors read is registered as a plain singleton by its plugin.
- The door net reads source text, so a door module whose comments spell one of the refused reader calls with its opening parenthesis also reds it; the shipped modules spell those names without one.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/own-door-bridge.test.ts` — expect `Tests 77 passed (77)`, with every case under "a dispatcher door is served only by the request's own kernel" passing.
